subject: SierraCloud marketplace integration - prioritization & product asks
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha@sierracloud.com>, partner-success@azuremarketplace.com
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: SierraCloud marketplace integration - prioritization & product asks

Team / Samantha,

Quick summary: SierraCloud wants to launch a private offer in the Azure marketplace and list Redwood as an integrated SaaS partner. They'd like an initial listing + private offer active by ~Apr 25 (Sierra's ask) but are flexible to Apr 28 if we need a few extra days. To hit this window we need a handful of product/engineering decisions this week and a short roadmap exception to bump the work into the next sprint.

Key asks from Sierra (see attached spec + draft MOP):
- Private Offer listing (Marketplace Private Offers) with metered billing support (usage reporting endpoint)
- SSO support at launch (SAML 2.0) for marketplace provisioning
- Listing metadata & branding assets (marketing will provide)
- DocuSign for procurement (Sierra will send)

Product/engineering questions for Redwood team:
1) Billing model: do we support metered usage for marketplace private offers out of the box, or do we require a subscription SKU? (Marissa)
2) Usage reporting: can we expose an Azure usage-reporting endpoint consistent with their spec, or is CSV/manual ingestion acceptable for GA? (Dev)
3) Provisioning flow: do we have an existing marketplace provisioning path (account-linking + provisioning webhook) or do we need a small extension in the Console/API? (Marissa/Dev)
4) Roadmap exception: can we re-prioritize one full-time engineer for ~3 weeks to own the integration + marketplace QA? (Laura to own partner comms)

Attachments: sierra_integration_spec_v1.pdf, draft_mop.xlsx

Samantha / partner-success: please confirm the specific marketplace contact for listings and whether Sierra requires any additional security attestations for the private offer (SOC2 evidence, etc.).

Asks from internal side: please reply with a short decision on the four questions above by EOD Mon (Mar 30). If we can't meet the Apr window, say so and propose the earliest realistic date.

Thanks,
Karthik
SVP, Partnerships & GTM
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha@sierracloud.com>, partner-success@azuremarketplace.com
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SierraCloud marketplace integration - prioritization & product asks

Karthik / team,

Thanks — quick answers and caveats below.

1) Billing model: Redwood's catalog currently supports subscription SKUs and a metered usage surface, but metered billing for a marketplace private offer requires integration with the marketplace usage API (we don't have an Azure usage exporter in GA). We can support metered pricing, but it will require engineering work to push usage to Azure or accept reconciled invoices.

2) Provisioning flow: we have a generic account-link flow and an OAuth-like grant for some partners, but Marketplace private offers expect a provisioning webhook and a return flow that updates the customer's console workspace. That will need a small Console + API change (UI for linking / a webhook endpoint).

3) SSO: we support SAML/SCIM for enterprise customers today, but marketplace-provisioned SSO needs a couple of mappings in our onboarding flow (automated vs manual SAML upload).

Timeline / tradeoffs: we can bump this into the next sprint but only if we defer a planned work item (caching/A/B throughput experiment). If stakes are high, I can approve the roadmap exception — but we need firm requirements from Sierra (billing model and SSO requirement) by Tue (Mar 30) so engineering isn't blocked.

I can own product specs and small Console UI changes. Dev — can you estimate effort (minimal/standard/full) for usage exporter + provisioning webhook?

-Marissa
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SierraCloud marketplace integration - prioritization & product asks

Marissa / Karthik — read the spec and sketched a couple of options. TL;DR: feasible, but scope matters.

Option A (GA-grade automated):
- Implement Azure usage reporting endpoint (ingest and forward usage to Azure Marketplace in their expected format) — ~2 sprints (including tests + infra)
- Add provisioning webhook + Console link support — ~1 sprint
- SAML onboarding tweaks — ~1 sprint (but lower priority if Sierra can upload IdP metadata manually initially)

Total: ~4 sprints for fully automated integration. Risk: pushes out ongoing infra work.

Option B (fast-follower / limited GA):
- Manual CSV ingestion or reconciled billing for first release (we produce usage CSVs on a cadence) — shipable in 1 sprint
- Minimal provisioning: manual acceptance flow + instructions to Sierra engineers — 1 sprint for Console UI polish
- SAML manual upload for early customers

Total: ~2 sprints to get a working private-offer listing and satisfy procurement; automated usage exporter can follow in a subsequent release.

Attachments: I attached a quick draft MOP (draft_mop.xlsx) and a slightly annotated integration spec (sierra_integration_spec_v1.pdf) highlighting required endpoints and sample payloads.

One blocker: need a Sierra test tenant and Azure marketplace sandbox credentials to validate end-to-end. Samantha — can you share test access and the Azure listing rep?

-Dev
Senior Engineer, Integrations
Redwood Inference

Hi Karthik / team,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from Sierra's side:
- Private offer is required for our procurement process (we need the private offer flow to be enabled).
- Metered billing is preferred, but if Redwood can't ship automated usage reporting immediately, we can accept CSV-based usage reconciliation for the first 60 days.
- SSO (SAML) is required at launch — customers often expect single-sign provisioning via marketplace. If there are mapping limitations, we can accept manual IdP metadata uploads for the first customers, but automated SAML provisioning would be preferred later.

Test assets and contacts:
- Azure marketplace sandbox rep: partner-success@azuremarketplace.com
- Sierra test tenant: https://sandbox.sierracloud.com/tenant/REDWOOD-TEST (creds to follow in separate, encrypted email)
- Procurement / DocuSign lead: contracts@sierracloud.com (they will send the DocuSign envelope for the private offer)

Timeline: we prefer Apr 25 but will accept Apr 28. If Redwood can commit to the Apr 28 date for a minimally viable listing (Option B from Dev), we will prioritize internal sign-off.

Samantha Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, SierraCloud
samantha@sierracloud.com

Team —

Thanks for the quick input. Summary and next steps (mutual action plan):

Decisions:
- We will go with Option B (fast-follow) for the initial private-offer listing: manual CSV reconciliation + minimal provisioning UI, SAML manual upload for first customers. This meets Sierra's acceptance criteria and gets us to market faster.
- Roadmap exception approved: Marissa will deprioritize the caching A/B experiment and allocate the slot; Dev gets a 3-week allocation starting next sprint to implement the Console link + manual CSV exporter.

Owners / deliverables:
- Dev Patel: implement manual CSV usage export and provisioning webhook stub; test with Sierra sandbox (owner) — due Apr 15
- Marissa Cole: finalize product spec for Console linking + onboarding instructions; update Console copy for marketplace flows — due Apr 8
- Laura Bennett: own partner communications, intake DocuSign, coordinate with Sierra procurement & Azure rep — due Apr 2
- Karthik: track launch milestone and confirm HubSpot deal (D-8342) updates; coordinate exec sign-off if anyone needs an SLA exception.

Related links: MAP draft -> https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A2b3C_sierra-map

Laura — please confirm you own the DocuSign follow-up and send the first envelope to contracts@sierracloud.com. Dev — once you have sandbox creds, loop me in if you hit infra blockers; we can escalate.

If everyone agrees, I'll mark the deal plan and schedule a 30-minute sync with Sierra next Tue.

—Karthik
